Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

fascinate verb

also fascinated, fascinating, captivate, enthral, hold someone’s attention

classical

Cic. Fin. 5.48: pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs teneantur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Ac. 2.20: ut oculī pictūrā teneantur, aurēs cantibus (Lewis & Short)

teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum

verb, second conjugation

hold; hold the attention of, fascinate

In this sense mostly passive: to be held, enchained by a sight or a sound (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • capiō, capere, cēpī, captum — captivate, charm

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.15: quod capiat ignārōs (Lewis & Short)

    To win someone over, often with the ablative of what does it (Lewis & Short).

  • fascinō, fascināre — bewitch, cast the evil eye on

    verb, first conjugation · avoid · classical · Verg. E. 3.103 (Lewis & Short)

    A false friend: classically to bewitch by an evil eye or tongue, not to interest (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ut pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs teneantur ob eamque rem vel famem et sitim perferant

    (children) are so held by a parade, games and such shows that for their sake they will bear even hunger and thirstCic. Fin. 5.48

  • nesciō quis tenerōs oculus mihi fascinat agnōs

    some eye or other is bewitching my tender lambsVerg. E. 3.103 (Lewis & Short)

See also interest.
